title: "Kloge Søren" (Søren Christensen), his Cyprianus, a book of charms in his own cipher, c. 1858 (catalogue 2525, KB Copenhagen, DFS 1997/020): simple substitution validated on a held-out portion, read in part

documents.shelfmark: Copenhagen, Det Kgl. Bibliotek, Dansk Folkemindesamling, DFS 1997/020 (Kloge Sørens samling); KB Digitale samlinger object392246, IIIF DFS_1997_020_4_000a to _107
documents.route: Søren Christensen, "Kloge Søren" (1843-1925), cunning man of Funen, writer and owner; a working book, not a letter

plaintext.source: no decipherment exists; the writer's own table of the cipher alphabet is on image 091 left

transcription.source: KB Digitale samlinger / IIIF images, 4,115 px per opening (first session) and full size 4,115 x 6,804 px per page (second session); images not reproduced
transcription.notes: Claude Opus 5.5 agents, 11 Nov 2026. Training pages 003 R - 007 L and the held-out images 030-031 transcribed sign by sign (notation in transcription.txt; the held-out files frozen and hashed before decoding). The 136 full-resolution pages were read straight into letters with the validated key, unresolved words kept in sign shapes (decryption.txt, Part 3). Two blind sheets of sign shapes answered by Brice Dudout: K1 (image 031) and K3 (nine targeted signs of the rest of the book); K2 (a random draw) abandoned before it was shown. Length counted in cipher words by the reading rule (8,055); signs counted only for the training portion (1,591) and the held-out portion (790).

system.summary: A private sign alphabet of the writer: one sign per letter, word spaces kept. Chevrons (a, e dotted), bars under 1-3 dots (u, n, m), strokes with dots above, beside or below (s, k, h, b, p), hooks (d, g, r, i/j), a cross (t, also f), an arch (v), dots (o, ø); ligatures aa, tt, nn, mm. Headings partly in clear Danish.
system.notes: Homophony or confusion t/f (cross), o/ø, i/j. The writer's table on image 091 left gives the alphabet a to ø in order. A circular seal in the same signs (018 R, 019 R, 104) is not read.

prior_solution.where: Catalogue 2525 vetting (Daniel Bourdeau, 11 Nov 2026): DECODE, Tomokiyo, Lasry nothing; no edition. Known: the book and its 'kodeskrift' (lex.dk, B. Rørbye; heuschkel.dk), not read. Rørbye, Kloge folk og skidtfolk (1976) not seen.

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose the target and set the rules (every decipherment goes to Daniel; a partial reading may be published if explained; protocol hashed before one single measurement; blind re-reading by sign shapes), and answered the blind sheets K1 and K3. Claude Opus 5.5 agents transcribed, found and validated the key, read and wrote up.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout (transcription, key, annealing, protocol, measurement, reading by 16 sub-agents, write-up)

solution.what: Training pages 003 R - 007 L transcribed sign by sign at 4,115 px (1,591 signs); word spaces found visible.

Key from the cribs '3 gange', 'i Navnet Gud Fader, Gud Søn og Gud den Hellige Aand. Amen' and the cipher ordinals 'Andet / Tredie Begreb'; then a blind annealing (simple substitution, Danish quadrigrams with space, only the space fixed) found the plaintext by itself (6 of 10 restarts).

One pre-registered measurement on the held-out images 030-031 (790 signs, transcribed and hashed before decoding): COV 0.4025 vs best of 200 permuted keys 0.1089 and of 200 sign shuffles 0.1038; C1-C3 and S met (C1 narrowly).
Held-out portion read by sense: 85.8% at once; image 031 right lines 16-26 re-read at full resolution: 96.1% (after the measurement, not blind).

Blind re-reading by sign shapes (sheet K1: 28 questions, 2 controls passed), rule hashed before the sheet: held-out portion 94.97% by the rule as written, 94.41% with Brice Dudout's remarks (result B, retained, declared deviation). Frames too tight: 3 of 5 losses from segmentation.

Second session: the rest of the book (007 R, 008 R - 079 R, 098) read at full resolution by 16 sub-agents, one fiche per page: 6,438/673/76/264 of 7,451 words = 95.4%. Image 091 left found to be the writer's table of the alphabet, confirming the key. Whole book 95.2% of 8,055 words, before any blind re-reading of this session.

Targeted blind re-reading by sign shapes of the second session (sheet K3: 9 signs chosen for the words whose class depends on the answer + 2 controls passed; rule hashed before the sheet, SHA-256 0400d3cf...; answers 4fbf5ec1...). Three probable words became certain, two unresolved; one ('før', 033 L) gives 'fer' by the rule with Brice Dudout's remark (result B, retained, declared deviation) but 'før' by sense, kept doubtful. Whole book 95.16% -> 95.13% (B; A 95.12%), indicative only; held-out portion untouched. The random sheet K2 was abandoned before it was shown.

outcome.method_basis: The key was found from probable words (the trinitarian closing formula, the clear '3 gange', the cipher ordinals of the headings) and confirmed by a blind annealing that found the plaintext alone; it was validated once on held-out images transcribed and hashed beforehand, and is confirmed after the fact by the writer's own alphabet table on image 091 left.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Held-out portion (images 030-031) after the blind sheet K1, result B (retained): 133 certain + 36 probable = 169 of 179 words = 94.41%; result A (rule as written) 94.97%. Whole book after the targeted blind sheet K3, result B (retained): 6,866 + 797 = 7,663 of 8,055 = 95.1% (A 95.12%; 95.2% before K3): indicative only. Nine first-session pages (low resolution) 90.6%, still to re-read.

validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered single measurement (not docs/_validate.py): PROTOCOLE.md SHA-256 106f10c69168ee2aa1c5a1390c040351b512f40bb461b426f3984fd2292a7329, KEY.json 40bf4b2d..., scorer 530a86e5..., word list 5c295d99... (frozen/FREEZE.sha256); held-out RESERVE-p030.txt d56aef4d..., RESERVE-p031.txt d2d93503...; COV 0.4025 (C1 >= 0.40), permuted keys max 0.1089 (C2 +0.25), sign shuffles max 0.1038 (C3 +0.25), S met. Bias declared: the held-out portion was transcribed by an agent who knew the key; C1 narrowly met. Confirmed after the fact by the writer's alphabet table (image 091 left).

texts.label: Kloge Søren's Cyprianus (DFS 1997/020), the charms in cipher, c. 1858
texts.summary: The working book of a Danish cunning man of Funen: about a hundred charms and recipes against bleeding, wounds, colic, toothache, fever and other ills; protection of cattle, horses, poultry, butter and milk against witchcraft; pests summoned to the Thing; guns bound and men made proof against shot; fire conjured; winning at cards; and a long series against thieves. The directions for use, hidden in the cipher, are new.

reading_review.by: Claude Opus 5.5 agent for Brice Dudout
reading_review.note: Read as Danish sentences of the mid-19th century against decryption.txt: the charms construe (sacred precedent, 'saa sandt som ... saa sandt skal ...', trinitarian close, directions for use) and the English summaries follow; but the held-out portion is at 94.41% after one blind sheet (Brice Dudout answered the shapes), nine pages were read at low resolution only (90.6%), and the second session (95.4%) has had only one targeted blind sheet (K3, nine signs; whole book 95.1%, indicative); so grade B, read in part. No human read the whole reading.

outcome.notes: New reading: no earlier reading or key of this cipher is known. The key is reusable (key.tsv, CC BY 4.0). No image or derivative of the KB scans is included. A private 20th-century piece, not part of the grimoire, is excluded.
